s0.text: Direction: "The Route". Basak's own teal and petrol ink, matured: a calmer ground, tone instead of borders, Readex Pro kept. One route-rail motif is reused for the pass, the station list and progress.

s1.text: First launch: four onboarding pages built from the real components. The first says what Basak is — every transport company for your university in one place — then subscribe and pay, the daily ride and alerts, and the card. Then four short sign-up steps; a returning student signs in with Face ID or fingerprint.

s2.text: Home answers two questions: is my pass valid, and am I riding tomorrow? Dates and money are on the subscription tab. The card tab is what a supervisor reads off the student's phone: photo, validity, line, stop and today's ride on the face, everything else behind "كل التفاصيل".

s3.text: The 5-screen wizard becomes one builder. Chosen rows collapse to a line and stay visible; tap any to change it. Line + station are one gesture. Review is a confirm sheet, not another page.

s4.text: The subscription tab is about time and money: period, validity, amount, receipt. Each status gets one card with one action. The route is not repeated here beyond one row.

s5.text: Alerts are a page behind the Home bell, not a tab: grouped by day, unread = dot + weight, no category toggles. Help is a sheet whose support channels come from configuration.

s6.text: Cache first. Offline is a slim strip plus a "saved at" stamp, never a blocked screen. Errors stay inside the section that failed; the card and pass keep working.

t7.text: 08 · Term recap · one student, start to finish

s7.text: A new feature, drawn for discussion. At the end of a term the student taps through a story about their own rides and shares the last page. Egyptian and self-mocking, tied to their college, stop and line. This row is one student, Sara: Engineering, 62 ride days.

t8.text: 09 · Term recap · the system behind it

s8.text: The recap is assembled from rules, so it holds for any student: nine different people, the voice of each college, and what happens with one ride, a hundred, no returns, no college, or a student who only comes three days a week.

s9.text: Rating: one sheet at a good moment; its button hands over to the store's own review dialog (App Store on iPhone, Google Play on Android). No stars and no "do you like it?" of our own — both stores disallow that. Update: a sheet you can dismiss when it is optional, a full screen when it is required, and even then the card stays one tap away.

t10.text: 11 · The rest · screens and states found in the app

s10.text: The app's code was read against the canvas, and what was missing is here: password recovery, the forced password change, photo picking and cropping, the ride question when it is closed or not open, the supervisor contact sheet, the push explainer and banner, an empty catalogue, the one-day cash subscription, exhausted receipt attempts, missing transfer details, editing details, deleting the account, an unavailable card and a wrong-role account. The last board lists every other state and message with its exact words.

s11.text: The supervisor app, same system. Four tabs that mirror the student bar: the filled one is the scanner (the student's is the card it reads). One line and one trip are chosen once and apply everywhere. Home is the numbers the buses are planned on: how many are going and how many are returning, per trip, today and tomorrow. Trips is the people on one trip.

s12.text: One scanner, always showing which trip it is boarding. A successful scan returns to the camera by itself; only problems wait for a tap. A repeat scan is a calm notice, not an error. Offline scans are never presented as recorded.

s13.text: Sending is one path: who, what, confirm. Ready messages come from the server; a free-text message goes through the same confirm sheet. The monthly summary moves out of the tab bar into the account, where it is used once a month.

s14.text: Cache first, as on the student side. The header and bell stay in every state. Messages say what happened and who can fix it; nothing sends the supervisor to the admin dashboard.
